subject: Pilot acceptance hypotheses & exit gates (MAP draft)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kline <sarah.kline@novusdx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot acceptance hypotheses & exit gates (MAP draft)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Attached is a short MAP-style draft that focuses on what we need to prove during the 4-week pilot to move to a short-term production POC. High-level goals are: validate model quality on your triage prompts, ensure predictable latency under your throughput, and confirm data-handling meets your retention/audit needs.

Key items in the attachment (novusdx-map-worksheet.xlsx):
- Acceptance hypotheses (quality, latency, reliability)
- Concrete test cases and sample prompts (pilot-test-cases.md + sample prompt set)
- Exit gates: go / hold / rollback criteria and owner for each gate
- Proposed timeline with gating milestones and signoff owner

A few specific acceptance signals we recommend validating in this pilot:
- Functional quality: top-1 relevance >= 92% on the 120-case clinical triage set; false-positive hallucination rate < 3% measured on negative-control cases
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 300ms for single-turn triage requests at target concurrency (20 rps simulated)
- Throughput: sustained throughput >= 18 rps for 60s windows with <2% error rate
- Reliability: error budget <= 0.5% over a rolling 24h window
- Security & compliance: logging/audit hook present and verified for three sample events, and encryption key management verified for dev->staging flows

Please skim and tell us: (1) any acceptance criteria that are off-base for you, (2) missing test cases we should add, (3) owners for the signoffs. If you’re good, we’ll finalize and turn this into JIRA tasks and a short timeline doc.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Attachments: novusdx-map-worksheet.xlsx, pilot-test-cases.md, sample-prompt-set.jsonl

From: Sarah Kline <sarah.kline@novusdx.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novusdx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance hypotheses & exit gates (MAP draft)

Jordan —

Thanks for the draft. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we sign off on the MAP: 

1) The clinical triage set you referenced — is that the anonymized 120-case set we shared last quarter or a new curated set? We need to ensure it includes our edge-case notes (IDs 47-52).
2) Latency target looks aggressive given our on-prem routing (we will be sending requests through our interconnect). Can we add an opt-in target for both interconnect and AWS direct path?
3) For security/compliance we need explicit evidence for KMS integration in staging, and retention policy verification (we retain logs for 365 days).

I like the explicit go/hold/rollback buckets — can you add a simple ‘must have’ versus ‘nice to have’ label next to each acceptance test? That will speed internal approvals.

Happy to hop on a 30m call Monday to finalize if that helps.

—Sarah
Sarah Kline
Head of Product, Novus Diagnostics
sarah.kline@novusdx.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kline <sarah.kline@novusdx.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance hypotheses & exit gates (MAP draft)

Sarah —

Thanks for the quick read. Jordan — I made inline edits to the spreadsheet (link in related links) and added a column for "Priority" (must-have / nice-to-have). Summary of changes: 

- Clinical set: We will use Novus's anonymized 120-case set (including edge-case IDs 47-52). We will also seed 20 negative-control prompts to measure hallucination. (Must-have)
- Latency: Split into two rows: interconnect (target 95p <= 375ms) and AWS direct (95p <= 300ms). We call out variability tolerance windows. (Must-have for AWS direct path, opt-in for interconnect)
- Security: We added a short checklist for KMS integration verification steps and a required artifact (screenshot or proof of key policy) for signoff. (Must-have)
- Acceptance owner: Novus product signs quality gates; Redwood infra signs latency/reliability gates; Security/compliance signoff will be joint.

Next steps: Jordan to convert the MAP into a 6-task JIRA epic and schedule a 30m sync. Sarah — if you can confirm owners on your side (who will sign the quality gate), we can lock dates.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kline <sarah.kline@novusdx.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance hypotheses & exit gates (MAP draft)

Folks — quick technical additions from infra before we finalize: 

- Load test spec: we'll run three staged runs — baseline (5 rps), nominal (20 rps), spike (40 rps) with 60s sustain. Acceptance requires <=2% error rate across nominal, and P95 latency within the thresholds Marissa aligned.
- Deterministic regression tests: we'll run the 120-case clinical triage set + 12 curated negative controls on every build. Regression failure defined as >3-point drop in top-1 accuracy or hallucination rate increasing by 1.5x.
- Canary/rollback plan: if any must-have gate fails during the production cutover, automatic rollback to previous variant within 10 minutes and incident declared. Owner = Redwood infra (Karthik) for rollback ops.
- Telemetry: add a short list of required metrics (response_time_ms, error_code, model_version, prompt_id, kv_cache_hit). We'll provide a Grafana dashboard template and a short verification checklist.

I'll push the JIRA epic after Jordan creates it. Jordan — propose the go/no-go decision meeting for Friday 2026-11-20 so Novus has two weeks after the pilot to review artifacts.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Infra | Redwood Inference
